recap.label: Daily Recap
recap.periodEnd: Thu, Nov 5, 2026, 4:00 PM ET (that day's close)
recap.timezoneNote: All times below are shown in ET (America/New_York). Items marked headline were written only from the publisher's headline and summary.

driver.text: Per WSJ, U.S. stocks plunged as disappointment in two major chip designers' earnings and post-election fears about curbed data-center development caused a rout in artificial-intelligence companies (4:51 PM ET); the Nasdaq composite closed in correction territory in the market's worst day since last April's tariff turmoil (WSJ, 4:41 PM ET). MarketWatch reported the S&P 500 lost an estimated $2.9 trillion in market capitalization, the largest one-day loss of market value on record, and that Micron, Sandisk and other AI stocks fell sharply as Wall Street weighed the prospect of a slower AI buildout (4:32 PM ET). The Financial Times reported investors fear newly elected politicians will seek to slow data-center development (11:59 AM ET). Treasuries surged on haven demand (Bloomberg, 10:54 AM ET), and oil futures recovered some of the previous session's heavy losses as hopes held for a U.S.-Iran agreement (WSJ, 3:55 PM ET). Earlier in the day, Bloomberg reported Hong Kong stocks rebounding as investors rotated from hardware into discounted Chinese internet platforms.

cryptoDriver.text: The Block reported that Bitcoin and ether fell as the Nasdaq selloff hit crypto, triggering $1.03 billion in liquidations and erasing Bitcoin's post-election gains.

morning.label: Morning Brief
morning.timezoneNote: All times shown in ET (America/New_York). Items marked headline were written only from the publisher's headline and summary.

driver.text: Artificial-intelligence stocks continued to weaken globally as investors digested the Democratic sweep in the U.S. midterm elections (WSJ, 4:46 AM ET). Treasury and European bond yields fell, with U.S. yields at eight-week lows, as markets weighed the prospect of fiscal restraint under a divided government (WSJ, 5:15 AM ET). Chipmaker Qualcomm's earnings disappointed (WSJ). Bloomberg reported that large hyperscaler tech stocks rose as Democrats threaten to slow AI spending, though not all AI companies fared well. Bloomberg also reported that Hong Kong stocks are rebounding as investors rotate from hardware stocks into discounted Chinese internet platforms. Oil rose but stayed below $100 a barrel as traders weighed U.S.-Iran diplomacy (WSJ, 5:38 AM ET), after plunging on Wednesday as the Dow posted its best day in 18 months (MarketWatch).
